Theorem
[Weak sequential compactness]1. ch5:5.12\group chapter-5 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0097

↗ gt.def5.5.hilbert-space ↗ gt.thm5.7 ↗ gt.def5.10.weak-convergence Every bounded sequence in a Hilbert space has a weakly convergent subsequence.
Proof

Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0097 \sketch In a separable Hilbert space, diagonalize the scalar sequences $(x_j,y_m)$ over a countable dense set. Their limits define a bounded linear functional, represented by some $x$ through Theorem 9; density then gives $x_{j_k}\rightharpoonup x$. For a general Hilbert space, apply the separable argument to the closed span of the original sequence and use the orthogonal decomposition of the ambient space.

□
